correctness.rationale: The proof reduces complete-multipartite strong geodeticity to one-use length-two geodesic resources supplied by selected same-part pairs. For an N-1 candidate, every one-vertex deletion is analyzed. The non-singleton-omission case forces exactly one outside pair; the singleton-omission case forces either one non-singleton part, one size-two part with additional singletons, or exactly two size-two parts. This gives the four families and the stated counts. Exhaustive matching-based verification agrees through order ten.

value.rationale: The parameter is defined as an extremal problem over minimal strong geodetic sets and is NP-complete in general. Classifying equality and near-equality with graph order is therefore a natural boundary question. The theorem completely resolves values N and N-1 on all connected complete multipartite graphs and enumerates every N-1 maximum set, while identifying new singleton-driven multipartite extremizers.
